newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Air France, Alitalia sign cooperation pact. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Air France, Alitalia sign cooperation pact. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]

text.p: State airlines Air France and Alitalia said on Friday they had signed a deal under which they will cooperate on code sharing and in other areas in a bid to expand and cut costs in the face of tough private competition.
Air France said chairman Christian Blanc signed a letter of intent on Thursday with Alitalia chief executive Domenico Cempella. Alitalia later confirmed the agreement.

The move was also aimed at boosting the two airlines' competitiveness in the increasingly tough European skies and is the sort of alliance more airlines will probably make in the future, analysts said.
"The role of the global alliance in the airline business is going to be an increasing one," an analyst in London said.

The news comes ahead of the opening up of European skies on April 1, allowing national airlines the freedom to fly between virtually any two cities in Europe. It is also set in a context of large, far-reaching alliances between private airlines in the United States and other European countries. (Corrects to make clear that deregulation of European air market will not occur until April 1.)
Air France already cooperates with U.S. airline Delta, among others.

The two airlines said in identical statements they would try to find new ways to expand and deepen their cooperation in the future, but that for the time being the accord concerned only code-sharing on flights between France and Italy.

"With the will to reinforce and extend their partnership, this agreement will allow Air France and Alitalia to explore and optimise all possible synergies between the two companies in France, in Italy and other countries, notably in the fields of assistance and frequent-flyer programmes," they said.
The deal, whose first steps would go into effect on April 1, would preserve independent operations and policy decisions by both airlines.

"The agreement, leaving both companies their independence for commercial policy and operating costs, involves various essential elements which will be put in place progressively from April 1, 1997," they added.

Air France and Alitalia flights would be operated under a code-sharing agreement which would later lead to the possibility of reservations on an Air France flight being made at an Alitalia counter in an airport, or vice-versa.
This was particularly likely at the start of the accord on flights between Paris, Bologna, Turin and Venice, they said.

links between French and Italian provinces would be developed, for instance with code-sharing on Alitalia flights between Lyon and Milan or Air France flights between Strasbourg, Lyon and Rome, they added.
